context: Sales call with a cinema chain about a ticket scanner kit. Noa sells the kit. Facts: the kit costs 7,400 per site per year, installation takes 3 days, the pilot covers 2 sites for 60 days, the contract renews each January.

lines.text: Hi Gil, hi Tali, thanks for making the time today.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Hi Noa. We have six sites and the lines at the doors on Friday nights are the problem.
That is the case the kit was built for.

lines.speaker: Tali
lines.text: Before we go further, how much is the kit for one site?
It is 7,400 per site per year, and the pilot covers two sites.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: And how long does installation take, because we cannot close a screen room for a week.
Three days per site, done in the morning before the first show.

lines.speaker: Tali
lines.text: Our budget for this is 5,000 per site, so your price is well above that.
I hear you on the budget, the pilot lets you test the value first.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Our current vendor scans slowly and the staff stop using it, so we are looking around.
Slow scanning is exactly the thing the pilot would measure.

lines.speaker: Tali
lines.text: I need the contract to renew in January like our other tools, not in the middle of the year.
That works, the contract renews each January.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Fine, send the pilot terms for the two sites by Thursday.
I will send them by Thursday.

lines.speaker: Tali
lines.text: Then we are done for today.
